results.title: GPT-6.1 Terra: Cheaper Computer Use for AI Agents | FlowHunt
results.content:
## Key Takeaways

 Half the price. Terra costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, half of GPT-6.1 Sol and the GPT-5.6 Terra model it replaces, and a tenth of GPT-6 Astra.
 Near-flagship computer use. OpenAI says Terra matches GPT-6 Astra on the Agents’ Last Exam computer-use benchmark at a tenth of the per-token price.
 Faster and more accurate. It finished benchmark tasks more than three times faster than Astra and Sol, and its factual error rate fell from 53.6% to as low as 4.3%.
 Not a coding flagship. OpenAI still points to Sol and Astra for the hardest coding work.
 Route, don’t replace. The practical win is sending each step of a workflow to the cheapest model that can do it well.

## What Is GPT-6.1 Terra? [...] :   Through the OpenAI API, GPT-6.1 Terra costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, with cached input reported at $0.05 per million tokens. That is half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol ($2 and $10) and of the GPT-5.6 Terra model it replaces, and a tenth of GPT-6 Astra ($10 and $50).

:   GPT-6.1 Terra is available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users, and to developers through the OpenAI API under the model ID gpt-6.1-terra. [...] ## Bottom Line

GPT-6.1 Terra won’t top every leaderboard, and it isn’t meant to. What it does is bring computer use, reading screens and operating software, down to a price where it can run on everyday tasks instead of showcase projects. For anyone automating work across tools that were never built to be connected, that matters more than another benchmark record.

results.title: What Is GPT-6.1 Terra? OpenAI's New Model
results.content:
GPT-6 Astra — the flagship, still OpenAI's strongest for the hardest computer-use and engineering work, at premium prices.
 GPT-6.1 Sol — the model for complex, multistep coding and agentic work where depth matters more than cost.
 GPT-6.1 Terra — the fast, cheap workhorse for high-volume computer use: forms, invoices, proposals, technical drawings, and video edits, where price-per-task and speed win.

A practical pattern for agent builders: route routine, well-defined computer-use steps to Terra, and escalate only the hardest coding subtasks to Sol or Astra. With Terra priced at half of Sol, that kind of model routing is a real cost lever.
